key_concept: Eukaryotes have three RNA polymerases with fixed jobs: RNA polymerase I makes rRNAs, RNA polymerase II makes the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA), and RNA polymerase III makes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs.
steps: Precursor mRNA is the primary transcript of a eukaryotic structural gene. It is also called heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA).
In eukaryotes, transcription in the nucleus is divided among three RNA polymerases.
RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs: 28S, 18S and 5.8S.

RNA polymerase II transcribes hnRNA, the precursor of mRNA. This transcript is then capped with methyl guanosine triphosphate at the $5'$ end, tailed with poly-A at the $3'$ end, and spliced to remove introns, giving mature mRNA.
RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs.
So precursor mRNA is synthesized by RNA polymerase II.
why_not_others: RNA polymerase I makes rRNAs and RNA polymerase III makes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs. DNA polymerase replicates DNA and does not transcribe RNA at all.
common_trap: Students often mix up I and III, for example by linking all rRNAs to pol I and forgetting that 5S rRNA is made by pol III, or by assigning tRNA to pol II.
time_saving_tip: Memorise the sequence 'rRNA – mRNA – tRNA' as Pol I – II – III, matched in order.
